## DATA PRE-PROCESSING & CLEANING 
```{r}

#1. COLUMN NAMES 

pfin <- pfin %>% 
  clean_names() 

#2. Normalize school names (ppl cannot spell)
pfin <- pfin %>% 
  mutate( 
    school_clean = str_trim(what_is_the_name_of_your_high_school) %>% str_to_lower(), 
    what_is_the_name_of_your_high_school = case_when(
      school_clean %in% c("arlington high school", "arlington high scho", "hibat allah hade", "arlington heigh school", "arlington high", 
                          "arlington highschool", "arlington highschool ma", "a", "arlington hs", "ahs", "arlington") ~
      "Arlington High School", 
                          TRUE ~ str_to_title(school_clean)
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-school_clean)

#3. Q11 - Multiselect modification 
pfin <- pfin %>%
  # 1) Split Q11 into a list of selections
  mutate(
    q11_list = str_split(x11_your_monthly_loan_payments_are_based_on, ",\\s*")
  ) %>%
  # 2) Collapse each list to the letters only
  mutate(
    q11_letters = map_chr(q11_list, ~
                            str_extract(.x, "^[A-E]") %>% paste(collapse = ",")
    )
  ) %>%
  # 4) Extract the letter for all other x1* questions
  mutate(across(
    matches("^x(?:[1-9]|1[0-2])_") & !starts_with("x11_"),  # note the underscore is *after* the group
    ~ str_extract(., "^[A-E]"),
    .names = "{.col}_letter"
  ))  

#4. Select all columns that need grading / modification to letters 

col_map <- c(
  school            = "what_is_the_name_of_your_high_school",
  grade             = "what_is_your_grade_level",
  pfin_instruction  = "have_you_received_any_formal_instruction_related_to_personal_finance_in_school_e_g_budgeting_credit_loans_investing",
  importance_score  = "x_in_your_opinion_how_important_is_it_for_high_school_students_ages_14_18_to_learn_about_personal_finance",
  confidence_score  = "how_confident_do_you_feel_in_your_ability_to_make_basic_personal_finance_decisions_e_g_budgeting_saving_understanding_credit",
  q1  = "x1_what_s_the_most_important_first_step_in_setting_up_a_long_term_financial_plan_letter",
  q2  = "x2_what_s_a_good_example_of_using_automation_to_manage_your_personal_finances_letter",
  q3  = "x3_what_is_the_most_responsible_first_move_for_building_your_credit_letter",
  q4  = "x4_when_you_can_t_pay_off_your_credit_cards_in_full_what_s_the_smartest_strategy_to_reduce_your_debt_long_term_letter",
  q5  = "x5_if_you_invest_100_a_month_starting_at_age_21_and_earn_7_annually_what_would_your_account_balance_be_at_age_91_letter",
  q6  = "x6_which_of_these_statements_accurately_reflect_the_risks_associated_with_investing_letter",
  q7  = "x7_which_metric_best_helps_you_compare_the_cost_vs_benefit_of_college_borrowing_letter",
  q8  = "x8_what_s_the_most_efficient_method_to_eliminate_student_loan_debt_letter",
  q9  = "x9_what_consequences_are_likely_to_occur_if_you_default_on_your_student_loans_letter",
  q10 = "x10_when_reviewing_a_loan_application_lenders_usually_examine_the_following_core_areas_letter",
  q11 = "q11_letters",
  q12 = "x12_if_inflation_is_3_what_does_that_mean_for_your_personal_finances_letter"
)

# rename and select in one go 
pfin_clean <- pfin %>%
  # pick & rename by splicing in col_map
  select(all_of(col_map)) %>%
  rename_with(~ names(col_map), .cols = everything())

#5. ANSWER KEY 

answer_key <- c( 
  q1 = "A", 
  q2 = "B", 
    q3 = "B", 
    q4 = "C", 
    q5 = "C", 
    q6 = "E", 
    q7 = "C",
    q8 = "C", 
    q9 = "D", 
    q10 = "B",
    q11 = "B,D", 
    q12 = "C"
  )

#6. GRADE AND TOTAL SCORES
pfin_clean <- pfin_clean %>%
  # grade each question
  mutate(across(
    all_of(names(answer_key)), 
    ~ . == answer_key[cur_column()], 
    .names = "{.col}_correct"
  )) %>%
  # sum up the TRUEs (each coerces to 1) into total_score
  mutate(
    total_score = rowSums(across(ends_with("_correct")), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

#7. FINAL CLEANED DATASET 

pfin_final <- pfin_clean %>% 
  select(school, grade, pfin_instruction, importance_score, confidence_score, 
         q1, q2, q3, q4, q5, q6, q7, q8, q9, q10, q11, q12, total_score)

```

## EXPLORATORY DATA ANALYSIS & VISUALIZATIONS

```{r echo = FALSE} 

# Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

#1. IMPORTANCE SCORE VS. CONFIDENCE SCORE OVERLAY - DENSITY PROPORTION PLOT 

density_plot <- pfin_clean %>%
  select(importance_score, confidence_score) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = "metric",
               values_to = "score")

ggplot(density_plot, aes(x = score, fill = metric)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = ..density..),    # or y=..count.. if you want counts
    position = "identity",
    binwidth = 1,
    color = "black",
    size = 0.3,
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = NULL, 
    labels = c(
      confidence_score = "Confidence Score", 
      importance_score = "Importance Score"
    ), 
    values = c(
      confidence_score = "red", 
      importance_score = "blue"
    ), 
    guide = guide_legend(
      keywidth = unit(0.8, "lines"), 
      keyheight = unit(0.8, "lines"), 
      default.unit = "cm", 
      label.position = "right", 
      ncol = 1, 
      byrow = FALSE, 
      vjust = 0.5, 
      direction = "vertical", 
      title.position = "top"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:5) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0.0, 0.55, 0.05), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .05))) +
  labs(
    title    = "Financial Knowledge at Arlington High:",
    subtitle = "Importance vs. Confidence Score Distribution", 
    x        = "Score (1 = Low, 5 = High)",
    y        = "Proportion (of Total Surveyed)"
  ) +
  # 3) Theme tweaks
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    # center the plot title
    plot.title           = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle        = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    
    # darken & margin the axis text
    axis.text.x          = element_text(color = "gray20", margin = margin(t = 5)),
    axis.text.y          = element_text(color = "gray20", margin = margin(r = 5)),
    
    # add space between axis titles and ticks
    axis.title.x         = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title.y         = element_text(margin = margin(r = 10)),
    
    # legend inside top right
    legend.position      = c(0.05, 0.95),
    legend.justification = c(0, 1),
    legend.background    = element_rect(fill = alpha("white", 0.7), color = "black"),
    legend.margin = margin(t=6, r=6, b=6, l=6), 
    
    # remove legend title and adjust text size
    legend.title         = element_blank(),
    legend.text          = element_text(size = 10)
  )
```

```{r echo = FALSE}
#2. AGE DEMOGRAPHIC BREAKDOWN - WAFFLE PLOT, BY GRADE

# prepare a data.frame for geom_waffle
df_w <- pfin_final %>%
  mutate(
    grade = factor(
      grade,
      levels = c("Sophomore (10th)", "Junior (11th)", "Freshman (9th)", "Senior (12th)")
    )
  ) %>%
  count(grade) %>% 
  # percentage share 
  mutate ( 
    pct = n/sum(n), 
    label_pct = percent(pct, accuracy = 0.01)
    )

ggplot(df_w, aes(fill = grade, values = n)) +
  geom_waffle(
    n_rows   = 17,           # try sqrt(302)≈17, then tweak 
    size     = 0.25,         # gap between squares
    colour   = "white"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("skyblue","#E45756", "orange","lightgreen"), 
    labels =paste0(df_w$grade, "\n", df_w$label_pct), 
    breaks = df_w$grade
  ) +
  coord_equal() +            # force square cells
  labs(
    title    = "Grade Distribution of Survey Respondents",
    subtitle = "(Arlington High School)",
    fill     = NULL
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    # push the entire plot down a bit
    plot.margin       = margin(t = 20, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10),
    # center & space out your title/subtitle
    plot.title        = element_text(
      size   = 16,
      face   = "bold",
      hjust  = 0.5,
      margin = margin(t = 15, b = 5)
    ),
    plot.subtitle     = element_text(
      size   = 12,
      hjust  = 0.5,
      margin = margin(t = 5,  b = 10)
    ),
    
    # legend at bottom, one row, centered
    legend.position       = "bottom",
    legend.direction      = "horizontal",
    legend.justification  = "center",
    
    # size of the colored boxes
    legend.key.width      = unit(0.6, "cm"),
    legend.key.height     = unit(0.6, "cm"),
    
    # space *between* boxes
    legend.spacing.x      = unit(1.0, "cm"),
    
    # left‐align text against the boxes
    legend.text.align     = 0,
    legend.text           = element_text(size = 10)
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(
    nrow       = 1,
    byrow      = TRUE,
    label.hjust = 0
  ))

```

```{r echo= FALSE}

#3. PIE CHART: PROPORTION ACCESS TO FINANCIAL EDUCATION

# 1) Prepare proportions
pie_data <- pfin_final %>%
  count(pfin_instruction) %>%
  mutate(
    pct   = n / sum(n),
    label = percent(pct, accuracy = 1)
  )

# 2) Draw the pie
ggplot(pie_data, aes(x = 1, y = pct, fill = pfin_instruction)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8, color = "black") +        # width < 1 to shrink the circle
  coord_polar(theta = "y", start = 0) +           # basic pie layout
  geom_label(
    aes(label = label),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    show.legend = FALSE,
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name   = NULL,
    values = c(
      "No"      = "firebrick1",
      "Yes"     = "springgreen", 
      "Not sure" = "royalblue1"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Access to Financial Education",
    subtitle = "What proportion of students at AHS have received some kind of personal finance instruction?"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    # 2) MOVE legend to the right
    legend.position    = "right",
    legend.direction   = "vertical",
    legend.key.size    = unit(0.6, "cm"),
    legend.text        = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.title       = element_text(size = 11),
    
    # 3) CENTER titles
    plot.title         = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold", margin = margin(t=15, b = 5)),
    plot.subtitle      = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12, margin = margin(t= 5, b = 10)),
    
    # 4) SHIFT pie up by giving extra bottom margin
    plot.margin        = margin(t = 20, r = 30, b = 30, l = 100)
  )
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
#5. QUESTION DIFFICULTY RANKING (TOP 5)

# 1) compute pct_wrong & pull out the top 5
hard5 <- pfin_clean %>% 
  select(ends_with("_correct")) %>% 
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ mean(!.x, na.rm=TRUE))) %>% 
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to="question", values_to="pct_wrong") %>% 
  arrange(desc(pct_wrong)) %>% 
  slice(1:5) %>% 
  
  # 2) create your display labels
  mutate(
    q_num = case_when(
      question=="q11_correct" ~ "Q11",
      question=="q7_correct"  ~ "Q7" ,
      question=="q5_correct"  ~ "Q5" ,
      question=="q3_correct"  ~ "Q3" ,
      question=="q4_correct"  ~ "Q4"
    ),
    q_text = case_when(
      question=="q11_correct" ~ "Loan Interest Basis",
      question=="q7_correct"  ~ "College-Cost Metric",
      question=="q5_correct"  ~ "Future Balance",
      question=="q3_correct"  ~ "Credit Move",
      question=="q4_correct"  ~ "Credit-Card Strategy"
    )) %>% 
  mutate(
    q_num = fct_reorder(q_num, pct_wrong)) # not ordering (asc)
  
bar_cols <- c(
  Q11="#A80000", Q7="#E69F00", Q5="#56B4E9", Q3="#009E73", Q4="#F0E442"
)

ggplot(hard5, aes(x=pct_wrong, y=q_num, fill=q_num)) +
  # your horizontal bars
  geom_col(width=1, color = "black", show.legend=FALSE) +
  
  # long question text centered in the bar
  geom_text(aes(label=q_text), 
            x = hard5$pct_wrong/2, 
            color="white", 
            size=3.5, 
            hjust=0.5) +
  
  # percent label at the end of each bar
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(pct_wrong, accuracy=0.1)), 
            x    = hard5$pct_wrong, 
            color="black", 
            size = 3.5, 
            angle = -90, 
            vjust = -0.5, 
            hjust = 0.5) +
  
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0), limits = c(0, max(hard5$pct_wrong)*1.05)) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values=bar_cols) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Top 5 Hardest Questions (By Percentage Incorrect)",
    x     = NULL, 
    y     = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.line.x   = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x  = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x   = element_blank(),
    
    axis.line.y   = element_line(color = "black"),
    axis.ticks.y  = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y   = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10, color = "black"),
    
    panel.grid    = element_blank(),
    plot.margin   = margin(20,30,20,30),
    
    plot.title    = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 14)
  )
```
